meta.title: TACIP cross-sector reference crosswalk
meta.purpose: Index that lets a governance reader in any of the 16 CI sectors find relevant, transferable guidance for each practice — the 'index' role described in the profile's second discussion question.

by_reference.reference: NIST AI RMF (AI 100-1) + Generative AI Profile (AI 600-1)
by_reference.notes: Govern/Map/Measure/Manage backbone for the whole profile

by_reference.reference: NIST IR 8596 Cyber AI Profile (prelim draft Dec 2025)
by_reference.notes: Sibling document; reference to align and avoid duplication; comments closed Jan 30 2026

by_reference.reference: DHS/CISA Safety and Security Guidelines for Critical Infrastructure Owners and Operators (Apr 2024)
by_reference.notes: Organized around three AI risk types (attacks using AI; attacks on AI; design/implementation failures)

by_reference.reference: DHS Roles & Responsibilities Framework for AI in Critical Infrastructure (Nov 2024)
by_reference.notes: Governance-audience-friendly; recommends actions for five stakeholder groups

by_reference.reference: NIST SP 800-218A (SSDF for Generative AI)
by_reference.notes: Closest structural sibling since your profile is SSDF-inspired

by_reference.reference: ISO/IEC 42001 (AI management system) & ISO/IEC 23894 (AI risk)
by_reference.notes: Certifiable AI governance management system

by_reference.reference: MITRE ATLAS + NIST AI 100-2 (Adversarial ML taxonomy)
by_reference.notes: Threat taxonomy for AI systems; anchors incident analysis and validation

by_reference.reference: NERC CIP Standards
by_reference.notes: Mandatory for bulk electric system; does not cover distribution/DER

by_reference.reference: DOE C2M2 (Cybersecurity Capability Maturity Model)
by_reference.notes: Maturity-gradient model; travels well across sectors

by_reference.reference: DOE CESER Energy Sector Cybersecurity + NERC AI reliability guidance
by_reference.notes: NERC developing AI-for-reliability guidance

by_reference.reference: Treasury 'Managing AI-Specific Cybersecurity Risks in the Financial Services Sector' (Mar 2024)
by_reference.notes: Best-practice report; strong on third-party AI risk and talent gaps

by_reference.reference: NYDFS 23 NYCRR Part 500 + Oct 2024 AI guidance
by_reference.notes: AI-enabled social engineering; deepfake-resistant MFA; third-party diligence

by_reference.reference: FFIEC IT Examination Handbook
by_reference.notes: Established IT/security governance baseline

by_reference.reference: HHS 405(d) Health Industry Cybersecurity Practices (HICP)
by_reference.notes: Tiered by org size; good maturity-gradient model

by_reference.reference: FDA AI-Enabled Device Software Functions draft guidance (Jan 2025)
by_reference.notes: Total Product Life Cycle + Predetermined Change Control Plan (PCCP); lifecycle validation model

by_reference.reference: FDA Cybersecurity in Medical Devices premarket guidance (2025/26)
by_reference.notes: SPDF/SBOM; secure-by-design extended to training data and model artifacts

by_reference.reference: WaterISAC 12 Cybersecurity Fundamentals (Dec 2024)
by_reference.notes: Prioritized fundamentals; small-systems version available

by_reference.reference: EPA Guidance on Improving Cybersecurity at Water Systems (rev. Aug 2024)
by_reference.notes: Gap-assessment method; references CISA/NIST/AWWA

by_reference.reference: AWWA Water Sector Cybersecurity Risk Management Guidance + Assessment Tool
by_reference.notes: Free assessment tool mapping controls to risk

by_reference.reference: NIST SSDF SP 800-218 + 800-218A
by_reference.notes: Secure development lifecycle; structural sibling to your profile

by_reference.reference: NIST AI RMF + ISO/IEC 42001
by_reference.notes: General AI governance

by_reference.reference: CMMC / NIST SP 800-171 (DFARS final rule eff. Nov 2025)
by_reference.notes: 110 controls for CUI; C3PAO certification phasing in

by_reference.reference: NIST SP 800-161 (C-SCRM)
by_reference.notes: Cyber supply chain risk management; strong for practices 6 and 7

by_reference.reference: NDAA FY26 Sec. 1513 AI framework (in development)
by_reference.notes: Directs DoD to fold AI framework into DFARS/CMMC

by_reference.reference: CSRIC Best Practices
by_reference.notes: FCC advisory council reliability/security best practices

by_reference.reference: NIST IR 8183 Manufacturing Profile (CSF)
by_reference.notes: CSF profile tailored to manufacturing OT

by_reference.reference: ISA/IEC 62443
by_reference.notes: OT/ICS security standard usable across all OT-heavy sectors

by_reference.reference: NRC 10 CFR 73.54 + Reg. Guide 5.71
by_reference.notes: Rigorous cyber program requirements; strong defensive-architecture model

by_reference.reference: NEI 08-09 Cyber Security Plan
by_reference.notes: Template cyber security plan endorsed by NRC

by_reference.reference: TSA Security Directives (pipeline/rail/aviation)
by_reference.notes: Performance-based cyber requirements

by_reference.reference: Auto-ISAC Automotive Cybersecurity Best Practices + ISO/SAE 21434
by_reference.notes: Vehicle cybersecurity engineering lifecycle

by_reference.reference: FISMA / NIST SP 800-53 + FedRAMP
by_reference.notes: Control catalog underpinning most other frameworks

by_reference.reference: OMB M-24-10 (and successor AI memos)
by_reference.notes: Federal AI governance/risk management practices

by_reference.reference: CISA ChemLock + CFATS RBPS (authority lapsed Jul 2023)
by_reference.notes: Risk-based performance standards still cited as a model

by_reference.reference: FERC Security Program for Hydropower Projects
by_reference.notes: Physical + cyber security program requirements

by_reference.reference: SAFECOM Guidance + CISA Emergency Services Sector resources
by_reference.notes: Interoperable communications and continuity focus

by_reference.reference: Food & Ag-ISAC + FDA/USDA cyber guidance
by_reference.notes: Thin AI-specific guidance - flag as a gap your index fills

by_reference.reference: CISA Commercial Facilities Sector resources + NIST CSF 2.0
by_reference.notes: Few AI-specific refs - rely on cross-sector anchors
